parts:
Hi,
I have lots of different datasets that I want to "ovelay" onto a
single plot within a single file. The desired output can be seen
here:
http://people.brandeis.edu/~dcaffrey/tmp/desired.pdf

The problem is that I need to iterate over each dataset using a for
loop and the for loop insists on writing each plot to a separate page
when writing to pdfas shown here:
http://people.brandeis.edu/~dcaffrey/tmp/test.pdf
When writing to jpg or X11 the last plot overwrites all previous plots
generated within the loop.

Most of the code is pasted below, and I'd appreciate any suggestions.

Thanks,
Daniel

p <- ggplot(data) + scale_x_continuous('Non-synonymous polymorphisms /
CD length',limits=c(0,0.01))

p <- p + scale_y_continuous( 'Density',limits=c(0,300))

p <- p + opts(panel.background = theme_rect(size=0))

p <- p + opts(panel.grid.minor = theme_blank())

p <- p + opts (axis.text.x =
theme_text(hjust=1,size=7,colour="black"))

p <- p +
opts(axis.title.x=theme_text(size=10,colour="black",vjust=0))

p <- p + annotate("text",x=x,y=y,label="Gene sets:",vjust = -2, hjust
= 0,size = 4)

allRowsOfInterest <- c()

lastIndex <- length(gosOfInterest)
for (i in 1: length(gosOfInterest)){
columnName <-
paste("hasGoTermThatIsDescendentOf",gosOfInterest[i],sep="")
column <- which(names(data) == columnName)
data[,column] <- gsub("TRUE",preferredName[i],data[,column])
data[,column] <- gsub("FALSE","Other",data[,column])
rowsOfInterest <- which(data[,column] == preferredName[i])
allRowsOfInterest <- c(allRowsOfInterest , rowsOfInterest)
curData <- data[rowsOfInterest,]
y <- y-dec
#ITERATION 1 is written to page 1 of PDF
if (i==1){
pdf(file="test.pdf",onefile=TRUE)
one <- curData
p <- p + geom_density(aes(x=one
$nsNormBySize),linetype=2,colour=set[i]) +
annotate("text",x=x,y=y,label=preferredName[i],vjust = -2, hjust =
0,size = 4,colour=set[i])
print(p)
}
#For simplicity, lastIndex is 2 and these plots are written to
the 2nd page. I want them to be overlaid on top of the plots in the
1st page
if (i==lastIndex){
two <- curData
p <- p + geom_density(aes(x=two
$nsNormBySize),linetype=2,colour=set[i]) +
annotate("text",x=x,y=y,label=preferredName[i],vjust = -2, hjust =
0,size = 4,colour=set[i])
i <- i+1
rowsOfInterest <- unique(allRowsOfInterest)
#combined genes
combinedData <- data[rowsOfInterest,]
y <- y-dec
p <- p + geom_density(aes(x=combinedData
$nsNormBySize),colour=set[i]) + annotate("text",x=x,y=y,label="All
Gene sets",vjust = -2, hjust = 0,size = 4,colour=set[i])
#other genes
numOfRows <- dim(data)[1]
allRowNums <- seq(from=1,to=numOfRows,by=1)
matched <- allRowNums%in%allRowsOfInterest
allOtherData <- data[!matched,]
y <- y-dec
p <- p + geom_density(aes(x=allOtherData
$nsNormBySize),colour="black") + annotate("text",x=x,y=y,label="Rest
of genome",vjust = -2, hjust = 0,size = 4)
print(p)
}

}

Hi Daniel- ( i should have sent this to the whole list the first time)

I believe the whole thing can be shortened to this.

## your data set

values <- runif(500,min=0,max=2)
param1 <- c(rep(TRUE,300),rep(FALSE,200))
param2 <- c(rep(TRUE,200),rep(FALSE,300))
param3 <- c(rep(TRUE,50),rep(FALSE,450))
myDf <- data.frame(values,param1,param2,param3)

## my code deviates here
m.myDf <- melt(myDf, id.vars='values')
m.myDf <- m.myDf[which(m.myDf$value),]
ggplot( m.myDf, aes(x=values,color=variable) ) + geom_density()

You, of course, could put this in a pdf. And if you want your specific colors, then scale_color_manual() can give you this. 

The first thing to note is that overlaying as you were doing is the completely wrong paradigm with ggplot. 

Looking at m.myDf you'll see it actually is looking a bit akward with "values" and "value". What's going on here is that myDf is melted against the variable "values": melt moves each param variable, while keeping its original "values" column lined up,  into the "value" column (the melt default variable name for the values) while also creating a "variable" column which describes which param it is (as a factor variable). All three params treated this way are then stacked row-wise, within these 3 columns.  

Because your only computing the density on 'values' where 'value' of param is true, you can simply throw out wherever value==FALSE (ie keep which(value)). Then your data frame is already for ggplot.

A melted data frame is exactly what ggplot eats up. Learning to construct data frames and use melt is a huge part of using ggplot and worth the initial head scratching. I remember the first time I tried it. hehe. A rule of thumb, if it seems like too much code, it probably is. 

~James

This happens because of the limits you imposed on the x and y axis of
the graph. Apparently, the values of your remaining group lie outside
the imposed range. Here's a simple example to illustrate:

dd <- data.frame(x = rnorm(500))
ggplot(dd, aes(x = x)) + geom_density()
ggplot(dd, aes(x = x)) + geom_density() +
scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-2, 2))
Warning message:
Removed 17 rows containing missing values (stat_density).

The message informs you that 17 values were outside the interval -2 <=
x <= 2 that was used to generate the density estimate.
Your warning messages have a parallel interpretation.

parts: After fiddling 10 minutes with your data. I realized that this is because scale_continuous throws away data when using limits, as Dennis points out. You want to use coord_cartesian.
p <- ggplot( meltedDf, aes(x=nsNormBySize,color=variable) ) +
geom_density()
p <- p + scale_x_continuous('Non-synonymous polymorphisms / CD

length')

p <- p + scale_y_continuous('Density')
# next line causes error relating to length

p <- p + scale_colour_hue("Gene sets")

p + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 0.1), ylim = c(0, 350))

As to why the first level isn't plotted. Is being overploted by anyGO. See below

meltedDf2 <- meltedDf
meltedDf2$variable <- relevel(meltedDf2$variable, "anyGo")

p2 <- ggplot(meltedDf2, aes(x=nsNormBySize,color=variable) ) +
geom_density()

p2 <- p2 + scale_x_continuous('Non-synonymous polymorphisms / CD
length', breaks = seq(0, 0.01, 0.002))

p2 <- p2 + scale_y_continuous('Density')
# next line causes error relating to length

p2 <- p2 + scale_colour_hue("Gene sets")

p2 + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 0.01))

HTH

Luciano

library(ggplot2)
preferredName <- c("Interacts with other organisms","Response to other
organism","All gene sets","Rest of genome")

#get the data I want

"#")columnsWithGo <- grep ("hasGoTerm",names(data))
names(data)[columnsWithGo] <- preferredName[1:
(length(preferredName)-2)]

rowsWithAnyGo <- unique(rowsWithAnyGo[,1])

anyGo[rowsWithAnyGo] <- TRUE
noGo <- rep(TRUE,dim(data)[1])
noGo[rowsWithAnyGo] <- FALSE

#only need certain columns
combinedDf <- cbind(data[,c(10,columnsWithGo)],anyGo,noGo)

#melt
meltedDf <- melt(combinedDf,id="nsNormBySize")
meltedDf <- meltedDf[meltedDf$value,]

#plot
p <- ggplot( meltedDf, aes(x=nsNormBySize,color=variable) ) +
geom_density(linetype=2)

p <- p + scale_x_continuous('Non-synonymous polymorphisms / CD
length',limits=c(0,0.01))

p <- p + scale_y_continuous( 'Density',limits=c(0,300))

# next line causes error relating to length

$variable), labels = preferredName)


print(p)
ggsave("myPlot.pdf", p)
